findings.title: vectorElemMinSize floors a zero-dimension inner vector at 1 byte, but such an element…
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize floors a zero-dimension inner vector at 1 byte, but such an element really takes 0 bytes. The bound therefore rejects payloads that base decoded, and the test comment justifying the floor is false.

findings.title: The new head comment in unmarshalVector says 'every path below turns it into an…
findings.claim: The new head comment in unmarshalVector says 'every path below turns it into an allocation (make, reflect.MakeSlice)'. The array path allocates nothing, and the PR's own test comment says so.

findings.title: The pre-existing fast-path comment "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic…
findings.claim: The pre-existing fast-path comment "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path" is now stale: a non-nil empty payload with Dimensions>0 is rejected by the new bound before reaching the fast path or the generic path.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType now keeps the server's class name only for unknown basic types
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType now keeps the server's class name only for unknown basic types. Its other degrade-to-custom paths still return NewNativeType(TypeCustom) with an empty name: a malformed MapType and unparseable VectorType dimensions. Those still render as a bare 'custom()', which the commit says it eliminates.

findings.title: The new test helper makeVectorType duplicates the existing makeFloat32VectorType and…
findings.claim: The new test helper makeVectorType duplicates the existing makeFloat32VectorType and makeDoubleVectorType builders in the same file instead of replacing them.

findings.title: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating measures the process-wide runtime
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating measures the process-wide runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc, and its comment says only parallel siblings could pollute it. Background goroutines left by earlier tests in the package (sessions, timers, pools) also allocate during the window.

findings.title: Both commit messages break CONTRIBUTING
findings.claim: Both commit messages break CONTRIBUTING.md's required format. The short description is lowercase with a conventional-commit prefix (`fix(marshal): reject ...`), when it should start with a capital letter, and neither message has the `Patch by <authors>; reviewed by <Reviewers> for #####` trailer.

findings.title: Two bugfixes (a crash on Scan from peer-supplied vector dimensions, and a nil-Type…
findings.claim: Two bugfixes (a crash on Scan from peer-supplied vector dimensions, and a nil-Type panic) ship without a CHANGELOG.md entry, which CONTRIBUTING.md requires for bugfixes.

findings.title: The new bound repeats the exact fast-path guard `info
findings.claim: The new bound repeats the exact fast-path guard `info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil` in two adjacent blocks, so the safety of the fast paths' Dimensions*8 / Dimensions*4 multiplication depends on two separately-maintained identical conditions.

findings.title: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads' doc justifies non-narrowing by 'a vector…
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads' doc justifies non-narrowing by 'a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes, so each of these sits on or above the boundary', but the bound enforces N*elemMin bytes, and the 'null value' subtest is not on or above any boundary (the bound is skipped for nil).

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize is a third wire-size classifier on top of vectorFixedElemSize and…
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize is a third wire-size classifier on top of vectorFixedElemSize and isVectorVariableLengthType. Its recursion re-implements, for nested vectors, the variable-length rule that isVectorVariableLengthType already encodes.

findings.title: The nil-Type guard rebuilds a 'no Go type' error after VectorType
findings.claim: The nil-Type guard rebuilds a 'no Go type' error after VectorType.Zero() has already swallowed the real error from SubType.NewWithError(). The guard is a symptom patch, not a fix at the source.

findings.title: The change to keep the name of an unrecognised type is applied in only one of…
findings.claim: The change to keep the name of an unrecognised type is applied in only one of getCassandraLongType's degrade sites. The vector dimension-parse failure still returns a nameless NewNativeType(protoVer, TypeCustom).

findings.title: The getCassandraLongType change alters the TypeInfo returned for every unknown nested…
findings.claim: The getCassandraLongType change alters the TypeInfo returned for every unknown nested type (list/set/map/tuple/UDT elements, not only vectors). Its String() and Custom() values change, but the comment and commit frame it as error-message-only, and no test exercises the non-vector callers.

findings.title: The new test helper makeVectorType duplicates the existing…
findings.claim: The new test helper makeVectorType duplicates the existing makeDoubleVectorType/makeFloat32VectorType fixtures field for field. It also takes the element as two independent parameters (Type and Java class name) that can disagree.

findings.title: The new test comment claims the word-size-dependent dimensions make the wrap case "land…
findings.claim: The new test comment claims the word-size-dependent dimensions make the wrap case "land on a 32-bit target too", but the unit-tagged package that contains this test cannot compile for a 32-bit target.

findings.title: The PR says "Every new test fails against pristine marshal
findings.claim: The PR says "Every new test fails against pristine marshal.go/helpers.go", but several of the new tests and subtests pass against base. Their only base failure is that the package does not compile, because TestVectorElemMinSize references the new vectorElemMinSize.

findings.title: Commit 0276a66's message describes a one-byte-per-element floor that the code does not…
findings.claim: Commit 0276a66's message describes a one-byte-per-element floor that the code does not implement. It also says every element takes at least one byte, which is false for a zero-dimension fixed inner vector.

findings.title: For a nested vector, the new error at marshal
findings.claim: For a nested vector, the new error at marshal.go:1048 prints info.SubType with %v. The inner VectorType that getCassandraLongType builds has custom set to the bare prefix (helpers.go:271), and VectorType has no String method of its own, so the message reads "no Go type for element type custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)". The inner element type and its dimensions are dropped.

findings.title: The test comment says a null value cannot excuse negative dimensions, but that holds…
findings.claim: The test comment says a null value cannot excuse negative dimensions, but that holds only for single-pointer destinations. Unmarshal sends nullable destinations (such as **[]float32) to unmarshalNullable, which returns nil for NULL before unmarshalVector runs.

findings.title: The dimension bound now runs before destination validation, which changes which error a…
findings.claim: The dimension bound now runs before destination validation, which changes which error a caller sees. For an invalid destination (non-pointer, non-empty interface or unsupported kind) with a short or empty payload, Unmarshal now returns 'N dimensions do not fit in M bytes' instead of 'can not unmarshal into non-pointer %T' or 'Accepted types: *slice, *array, *any.'. A negative dimension also errors on a NULL value before the nil handling runs.

findings.title: The helpers
findings.claim: The helpers.go change affects every long-form parse, not just vector elements. Unknown element types inside lists, sets, maps, tuples, UDT fields and vectors now have Custom()==name and String()=='custom(<class>)' instead of '' and 'custom()', and the NativeType values no longer compare equal to NewNativeType(proto, TypeCustom). The PR body frames this only as vector error text.

findings.title: For the nested-vector case, the new error message cannot say what the element actually is
findings.claim: For the nested-vector case, the new error message cannot say what the element actually is. VectorType has no String method, so %v on info.SubType prints the embedded NativeType as 'custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)', without the inner element type or dimension. 'no Go type' is also misleading here: the same nested vector decodes into a concrete [][]float32.

findings.title: Both commits carry a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' trailer and the PR body ends with…
findings.claim: Both commits carry a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' trailer and the PR body ends with '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]'. The user's global instructions forbid Claude/Anthropic attribution in commits and PR descriptions.

findings.title: The nil-Zero guard comment and error text claim the element type "has no Go…
findings.claim: The nil-Zero guard comment and error text claim the element type "has no Go representation", but for the nested-vector case the test pins, the element does have one ([]float32); the nil comes from getCassandraLongType storing only the bare "...VectorType" prefix as the custom name, which asVectorType cannot parse.

findings.title: makeNestedVectorType builds a nested VectorType whose inner element carries the full…
findings.claim: makeNestedVectorType builds a nested VectorType whose inner element carries the full custom spec, unlike the wire-resolved nested type (bare prefix), so fixture-based and wire-based nested types behave differently on the same path.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize recognizes a nested vector only via a direct `elemType
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize recognizes a nested vector only via a direct `elemType.(VectorType)` assertion, adding another vector classifier alongside asVectorType (which also accepts a NativeType carrying a VectorType(...) custom name) and isVectorVariableLengthType's own recursion.

findings.title: The comment 'elemMin is the fewest bytes an element can occupy, so it bounds the count;…
findings.claim: The comment 'elemMin is the fewest bytes an element can occupy, so it bounds the count; unmarshalList does the same' overstates the parallel: unmarshalList uses a flat 4-byte floor only on the slice branch, not a per-element-type minimum, and not for arrays.

findings.title: For a nested vector, the new message says the element type has "no Go type"
findings.claim: For a nested vector, the new message says the element type has "no Go type". A nested vector does have a Go type ([][]T) and decodes into a concrete [][]float32 (test at marshal_vector_test.go:909-918). The real cause is a driver limitation, which the PR defers to #1085.

findings.title: The new dimension bound (marshal
findings.claim: The new dimension bound (marshal.go:997-1003) runs before the destination type is checked. A short payload scanned into an unsupported destination such as *int now returns "N dimensions do not fit in M bytes" instead of the sibling "can not unmarshal … Accepted types: *slice, *array, *any." (marshal.go:1118). A short payload into *[]float32 or *[]float64 now gets the bound message instead of the fast path's exact "expected X bytes, got Y".

findings.title: The new code comment and commit 0276a66 say the vector bound is what 'unmarshalList does…
findings.claim: The new code comment and commit 0276a66 say the vector bound is what 'unmarshalList does the same' or does 'the way unmarshalList already does'. unmarshalList bounds only slice destinations, divides by a flat 4 bytes per element, and reports "invalid size %d". The vector bound covers arrays and every destination, uses a recursive per-element minimum, and reports "%d dimensions do not fit in %d bytes".

findings.title: Commit 0276a66 changes behaviour so that a short or empty non-NULL payload now errors…
findings.claim: Commit 0276a66 changes behaviour so that a short or empty non-NULL payload now errors instead of decoding to zero values. A NULL value with negative dimensions also errors now (marshal.go:992-994 runs before the data==nil return). The commit message does not mention either change; only the PR body describes the short-payload case, and neither mentions the NULL case.

findings.title: The PR body says the bound sits 'ahead of every consumer' of the peer's Dimensions, but…
findings.claim: The PR body says the bound sits 'ahead of every consumer' of the peer's Dimensions, but the parsers that produce Dimensions are unchanged. frame.readTypeInfo still discards the Atoi error and yields dim 0 (frame.go:861), and getCassandraLongType accepts negative values. The PR depends on #1093 to reject dim < 1.

findings.title: A nested vector with a nonpositive inner dimension still receives the one-byte fallback,…
findings.claim: A nested vector with a nonpositive inner dimension still receives the one-byte fallback, so the outer bound can allow one claimed outer element per payload byte and allocate the entire outer slice before the inner decoder rejects the metadata.
